Bảng giá đất và hệ số điều chỉnh giá đất.title: Land Price Lists and Land Price Adjustment Coefficients 2026: What Homebuyers Need to Understand
Bảng giá đất và hệ số điều chỉnh giá đất.excerpt: The land price list and the K coefficient determine many payments when you buy or sell property, change land use purpose, or have land recovered. How to read them correctly under the 2026 rules in Hanoi.
content: When looking at a house or a plot of land, buyers usually care only about the asking price. But there is another price, set by the State, that quietly determines many amounts you must pay or receive: the
price in the land price list
, together with the
land price adjustment coefficient
(commonly called the K coefficient in Hanoi).
From 2026, these two tools are used more widely than before under
Resolution No. 254/2025/QH15
of the National Assembly. This article explains what they are, what they are used for, and how Hanoi is applying them.
What is the land price list?
The land price list is a table of prices set by the State for each
type of land
, by
area
and
location
. Where a digital cadastral map and a land price database exist, the list can go down to the level of individual land parcels (Clause 2, Article 7 of Resolution 254).
From 1 January 2026, the
provincial People's Council

decides the land price list and may amend and supplement it when needed (Clause 3, Article 7). Decree No. 49/2026/NĐ-CP lists the cases in which the list may be amended or supplemented, for example when administrative boundaries or street names change, or when a price needs to be added for a street not yet in the list (Article 6).
Keep in mind: the price in the list is
the price used to calculate obligations and entitlements toward the State
, not the actual transaction price between buyer and seller.
What is the land price list used for?
Clause 1, Article 7 of Resolution 254 lists the purposes for which the land price list serves as a basis. Below are the ones homebuyers are most likely to encounter.
Land use fees
When land is allocated, land use rights are recognized, or the use purpose is changed to residential land, the land use fee is calculated based on the area, the
price in the land price list and the adjustment coefficient
, exemption and reduction policies, and some other factors (Clause 1, Article 5). If the land is auctioned, the price used is the winning auction price.
Converting garden or pond land to residential land

For garden or pond land within the same parcel as residential land, the land use fee is calculated on the difference between the residential land price and the agricultural land price, both taken from the land price list:
for the portion within the allocation limit,
for the portion exceeding the limit by up to 1 times the limit, and
for the portion exceeding that (Point c, Clause 2, Article 10). The higher the price list, the larger this difference.
Taxes, fees and charges

The land price list is the basis for calculating taxes, fees and charges related to land use (Clause 1, Article 7). In a sale, the two familiar items are the seller's personal income tax and the buyer's registration fee. Which price is used for each item (the price stated in the contract or the price in the list) is governed separately by tax and fee law; buyers and sellers should ask the tax authority or a notary office how the calculation applies to their specific transaction.
Compensation when the State recovers land
Land compensation is calculated according to the
price in the land price list and the adjustment coefficient
(Clause 6, Article 3 and Clause 3, Article 5). The price of residential land at the resettlement site is calculated the same way.
What is the land price adjustment coefficient (K coefficient)?
Under Article 8 of Resolution 254, it is the
rate of increase or decrease
relative to the price in the land price list for each type of land, area and location. The
provincial People's Committee
issues the coefficients, applicable from 1 January each year, and may amend them during the year.
In simple terms:
price used for calculation = price in the land price list × coefficient
. A coefficient of 1 means the list price is kept as is. A coefficient above 1 means the price used is higher than the list price.
Decree No. 49/2026/NĐ-CP (Article 8) divides the coefficients into three types:
Market fluctuation coefficient

: the market price divided by the price in the land price list. The market price is the average of at least 3 sample land parcels that have been transferred, won at auction, or had their price approved by a competent authority.
Planning coefficient
: calculated according to the land type and the land use coefficient of the project.
Other-factor coefficient
: determined by the locality according to actual conditions.
How is Hanoi applying them?
Land price list: Resolution No. 52/2025/NQ-HĐND
The Hanoi City People's Council issued
Resolution No. 52/2025/NQ-HĐND dated 26 November 2025
on the first land price list, applicable from
1 January 2026

, published in the Hanoi Official Gazette. The list is divided by area, each area covering a group of wards and communes. For non-agricultural land, each street has prices for residential land, commercial and service land, and non-agricultural production and business land, each divided into 4 locations (VT1 to VT4).
Adjustment coefficient: Decision No. 19/2026/QĐ-UBND
The City People's Committee issued
Decision No. 19/2026/QĐ-UBND dated 2 February 2026
, effective the same day, based on Article 8 of Resolution 254. This decision repeals Article 1 of Decision No. 89/2025/QĐ-UBND. According to the content published on the Government portal:
For calculating
compensation
when the State recovers land:
For calculating
fees, taxes and charges
in the cases under Clause 1, Article 159 of the Land Law:

Industrial projects, industrial clusters, auction starting prices and some projects under Clause 1, Article 160 of the Land Law (without mixed purposes): market coefficient K = 1; planning coefficient in the form K = 1.x (the specific value of x is in the full text of Decision No. 19/2026/QĐ-UBND); other-factor coefficient

for projects using commercial and service land, new urban areas, auction areas, and commercial housing areas near administrative, commercial, cultural and sports centers, educational facilities, parks, entertainment areas and scenic sites, and K = 1 for the rest.
For most individual residential transactions, K = 1 means
the price used is exactly the price in the land price list
. To find the specific figure, look up the street name, street section and land parcel location in the appendix of Resolution 52.
Quick summary
Land price list (general framework)
— Effective date: 1 January 2026; Decided by: provincial People's Council (Article 7 of Resolution 254); Applies to: Land use fees, land lease, taxes and fees, compensation, auction starting prices
Land price adjustment coefficient (general framework)
— Effective date: 1 January each year; Decided by: provincial People's Committee (Article 8 of Resolution 254); Applies to: Upward or downward adjustment relative to the list price
How coefficients are calculated
— Effective date: 31 January 2026; Decided by: Government (Article 8 of Decree 49/2026); Applies to: Three types of coefficients: market, planning, other factors
Hanoi land price list
— Effective date: 1 January 2026; Decided by: Hanoi People's Council (Resolution 52/2025/NQ-HĐND); Applies to: Prices by street and location in Hanoi
Hanoi K coefficient
— Effective date: 2 February 2026; Decided by: Hanoi People's Committee (Decision 19/2026/QĐ-UBND); Applies to: K = 1 for compensation and fees, taxes and charges; separate levels for some projects
What homebuyers should do
Identify the land parcel's
ward or commune
, street, and location VT1 to VT4, then look up the corresponding appendix of the land price list.
Check the
K coefficient currently in force
on the date of signing the contract or the date of the decision, because the People's Committee may amend the coefficient during the year.
Ask the tax authority or a notary office how to calculate personal income tax and registration fees correctly for your transaction.
Land with garden or pond areas: first work out the difference between the residential and agricultural land prices according to the land price list.
Buying a home in a project: ask the developer about the project's status in completing its land-related financial obligations.
If you are considering a home in the Ciputra area, Phú Thượng, you can
view the projects Tami distributes at Ciputra
such as Maison Privée, Astor 1 and The Windsor Collection for specific advice.
Reference documents

dated 11 December 2025 of the
National Assembly
on certain mechanisms and policies to resolve difficulties and obstacles in implementing the Land Law, effective from 1 January 2026.
Decree No. 49/2026/NĐ-CP
dated 31 January 2026 of the
Government
detailing and guiding the implementation of a number of articles of Resolution 254/2025/QH15. Full text:
Government Electronic Portal

dated 26 November 2025 of the
Hanoi City People's Council
on the first Land Price List to be announced and applied from 1 January 2026. Version published in the Hanoi Official Gazette (issues 393+394, appendix for area 2):
datafiles.hanoi.gov.vn

dated 2 February 2026 of the

on promulgating the land price adjustment coefficients in Hanoi City:
vanban.hanoi.gov.vn
; content summary at
xaydungchinhsach.chinhphu.vn

of the

(as amended and supplemented). Look up at:

Dự thảo Luật Đất đai (sửa đổi) 2026: nhữ.title: Draft Land Law (Amended) 2026: Notable Proposals
Dự thảo Luật Đất đai (sửa đổi) 2026: nhữ.excerpt: The draft amended Land Law is being discussed by the National Assembly at its 2nd Session (October 2026). What could change for homebuyers?
content: This is a draft, not yet law.

On the morning of 22 October 2026, at the 2nd Session of the 16th National Assembly, the Government submitted the draft amended Land Law and the National Assembly discussed it in group sessions. As of 23 October 2026, the National Assembly had
not yet voted to adopt it
. Land Law No. 31/2024/QH15 remains in force and is the basis for all current transactions. This article summarizes the proposals that directly affect buyers of homes and land.
Where does the draft stand?
Drafting agency:
the Ministry of Agriculture and Environment. The draft was released for public comment before being submitted to the National Assembly.
Government direction to finalize:
Resolution No. 278/NQ-CP dated 18 September 2026 required the dossier to be finalized urgently for submission to the National Assembly at the 2nd Session.
Examination:
the National Assembly's Committee on Economic and Financial Affairs carried out a preliminary examination on 29 September 2026 and submitted its formal examination report on 22 October 2026.
Submission to the National Assembly:

On the morning of 22 October 2026, Minister of Justice Hoàng Thanh Tùng, on behalf of the Prime Minister, presented a joint submission for three draft laws: the Land Law, the Housing Law and the Law on Real Estate Business (amended). The National Assembly discussed them in group sessions that morning and afternoon.
Vote:
has not yet taken place. The National Assembly will consider adoption during the 2nd Session; readers should follow the National Assembly's press releases for the official outcome.
In terms of scale, the version submitted to the National Assembly has
13 chapters and 112 articles
, which is 3 chapters and 148 articles fewer than the 2024 Law. Details on procedures are delegated to the Government to regulate.
Notable proposals for buyers
1. Land prices: dropping the "specific land price" and using the land price list plus an adjustment coefficient

According to the submission, the draft does not retain the specific land price mechanism or consulting organizations that determine land prices. Instead, land use fees, land rent and compensation would be calculated according to the
land price list combined with the land price adjustment coefficient
. The draft sets out the principles and bases for State land valuation, and the land price list.

For buyers, the State land price is the basis for calculating financial obligations, for example when changing the land use purpose or when land use rights are recognized. It is not the market transaction price.
2. Identification code for each land parcel, electronic certificates
Each land parcel would have
a single nationwide identification code
. Land registration and the Certificate, whether in paper or electronic form, would have
equal legal value
. According to the submission, state agencies may not require citizens or businesses to provide again information that is already in the database.
3. Notarization: the Government will specify which contracts must be notarized

Current law requires contracts for the transfer, donation, mortgage or capital contribution of land use rights to be notarized or certified, except in real estate business cases. According to the submission, the draft assigns
the Government to determine which types of contracts must be notarized or certified
, linked to the digital transformation roadmap. The specific list is therefore not in the draft law.
4. Considering issuance of certificates for procedural violations before 1 August 2024
According to the submission, the draft proposes considering the issuance of Certificates in certain cases of
procedural violations before 1 August 2024
, provided the land has been used stably, is not in dispute and conforms to planning.
5. Projects slow to use land: progressive payments, recovery after 60 months
For projects that do not put land into use or fall behind schedule, the submission proposes collecting a
progressive payment that increases with the length of the violation
. After
60 months

without the land being put into use, the State would recover it. This proposal aims to force developers to proceed on schedule, indirectly reducing the risk of "stalled projects" for buyers of off-plan homes. The submission does not state specific progressive rates.
6. Land rent paid in one lump sum or annually, decentralized to the commune level

Those leasing land may choose to pay rent in one lump sum or annually. Under the decentralization approach, communes handle households, individuals and residential communities; the provincial level handles organizations and projects located across two or more commune-level administrative units.
Current law vs. the draft
Scale
— Land Law 2024 (in force): 16 chapters, 260 articles; Draft Land Law (amended), submitted to the National Assembly on 22 October 2026: 13 chapters, 112 articles
Land price for financial obligations

— Land Law 2024 (in force): Land price list and specific land price (Articles 159, 160); Draft Land Law (amended), submitted to the National Assembly on 22 October 2026: Drops the specific land price, uses the land price list plus an adjustment coefficient
Certificate

— Land Law 2024 (in force): Issued in a uniform form; Draft Land Law (amended), submitted to the National Assembly on 22 October 2026: Paper and electronic forms have equal value, with a land parcel identification code
Notarization of transfer contracts

— Land Law 2024 (in force): Notarization or certification mandatory, except in real estate business cases (Clause 3, Article 27); Draft Land Law (amended), submitted to the National Assembly on 22 October 2026: The Government specifies which contracts must be notarized or certified
Projects slow to put land into use

— Land Law 2024 (in force): Extension of 24 months and a payment for the delay period; recovery on expiry (Clause 8, Article 81); Draft Land Law (amended), submitted to the National Assembly on 22 October 2026: Progressive payment according to the violation period; recovery after 60 months
Effect

— Land Law 2024 (in force): From 1 August 2024; Draft Land Law (amended), submitted to the National Assembly on 22 October 2026: Not yet in force; the effective date will be decided by the National Assembly upon adoption
What homebuyers should note
All current transactions are still carried out under the
2024 Land Law
and its guiding documents. Do not apply the content of the draft.
Dossiers in progress (certificate issuance, transfer of ownership, change of purpose) should be
completed under current regulations
. The transitional provisions of the new law have not been finalized.
If a developer or seller cites the "new law" to change contract terms, ask them to specify the document that has been
adopted and is in force
Follow the National Assembly's vote result and the official date the law takes effect.
When buying an off-plan home, check the project's land use progress and legal status right now.
Reference documents
Land Law No. 31/2024/QH15
, National Assembly, dated 18 January 2024 (in force from 1 August 2024 under Law No. 43/2024/QH15). Look up at: https://vanban.chinhphu.vn/?pageid=27160&docid=211189
dated 29 June 2024, National Assembly: https://vanban.chinhphu.vn/?pageid=27160&docid=211201
Resolution No. 278/NQ-CP dated 18 September 2026

of the Government on the September 2026 thematic meeting on law-making: https://xaydungchinhsach.chinhphu.vn/chinh-phu-yeu-cau-khan-truong-hoan-thien-cac-du-an-luat-dat-dai-nha-o-kinh-doanh-bat-dong-san-sua-doi-119260920101326422.htm
Preliminary examination of the draft Land Law (amended)

, Committee on Economic and Financial Affairs, 29 September 2026 (People's Representative Newspaper): https://daibieunhandan.vn/tham-tra-so-bo-du-an-luat-dat-dai-sua-doi-va-du-an-luat-kinh-doanh-bat-dong-san-sua-doi-10432172.html
Submission on the draft Land Law (amended)

to the National Assembly on 22 October 2026 (Government Electronic Newspaper): https://baochinhphu.vn/thao-go-cac-diem-nghen-ve-the-che-giai-phong-nguon-luc-dat-dai-cho-phat-trien-kinh-te-xa-hoi-102261022091715919.htm
Press Release No. 06, 2nd Session, 16th National Assembly
(People's Representative Newspaper), 22 October 2026: https://daibieunhandan.vn/thong-cao-bao-chi-so-06-ky-hop-thu-2-quoc-hoi-khoa-xvi-10439539.html

This article is general information compiled from legal documents and publicly available drafts and does not replace legal advice. The content of the draft may change when the National Assembly adopts it. Updated on 23 October 2026.

Luật Kinh doanh bất động sản (sửa đổi):.title: Law on Real Estate Business (Amended): Fewer Business Conditions, Stronger Buyer Protection
Luật Kinh doanh bất động sản (sửa đổi):.excerpt: The draft amended Law on Real Estate Business is before the National Assembly: simpler business conditions and a new 5% security mechanism for buyers.
content: This is a draft before the National Assembly, not yet law.

On the morning of 22 October 2026, at the 2nd Session of the 16th National Assembly, the Government submitted the draft amended Law on Real Estate Business. The Committee on Economic and Financial Affairs presented its examination report. As of 23 October 2026, the National Assembly had
not yet voted
. All current home purchase contracts are still governed by
Law on Real Estate Business No. 29/2023/QH15
Progress of the draft law
Drafting agency:
the Ministry of Construction. The draft dossier was posted for public comment on the Ministry's portal from early July 2026.
Government direction to finalize:
Resolution No. 278/NQ-CP dated 18 September 2026 assigned the Minister of Construction to finalize the dossier for submission to the National Assembly at the 2nd Session.
Examination:
the Committee on Economic and Financial Affairs carried out a preliminary examination on 29 September 2026 and presented its examination report to the National Assembly on 22 October 2026.
Submission to the National Assembly:
On 22 October 2026, Minister of Justice Hoàng Thanh Tùng, on behalf of the Prime Minister, presented the submission. The National Assembly discussed it in group sessions that day.
Vote:
has not yet taken place. The National Assembly will consider adoption during the 2nd Session; readers should follow the National Assembly's press releases for the official outcome.
The draft has
10 chapters and 61 articles
, 22 fewer than the 2023 Law (83 articles). According to the submission, the draft
cuts 4 of 12 administrative procedures
, reviews and streamlines and shortens the processing time of 7 of 12 procedures, and
cuts or simplifies 9 of 31 business investment conditions
Notable proposals
1. Security for the final 5% of the contract

This is the most notable new point for buyers of off-plan homes. Current law allows the developer to collect at most 95% of the contract value before the buyer is issued a certificate. The draft adds a
security mechanism for the remaining 5% of the value
: this amount would be paid into a
blocked account
or handled as agreed by the parties. The examination committee recommends that the law clearly set out the principles for managing the money in the account and how risks are handled.
2. Deposits: still capped at 5%, recommended to be separated from capital mobilization
The draft published by the Ministry of Construction in July 2026 keeps the principle: the developer may receive a deposit of
at most 5% of the sale price
only when the home meets the conditions to be put on sale. The deposit agreement must state the sale price clearly (Clause 5, Article 18). The examination committee recommends
clearly distinguishing deposits from capital mobilization
, while also controlling other payments that are in essence capital mobilization before the permitted time.
3. A bank guarantee remains a condition before sales launch
Under the July 2026 draft (Article 20), before selling or leasing-to-purchase an off-plan home, the developer must still obtain a bank's agreement to issue a guarantee. The seller
may not collect 100% of the contract value
before the buyer is issued a Certificate. The specific payment thresholds in the final version will be determined when the National Assembly adopts the law.
4. Notarization and standard contracts
The July 2026 draft keeps the approach of current law. Contracts in which at least one party is a real estate business enterprise are notarized
at the request of the parties
. Contracts between individuals
must be notarized or certified

(Article 33). The developer must publish its standard contract on the Housing and Real Estate Market Information System before using it (Article 34). The examination committee recommends that the Government identify which cases truly need notarization and harmonize this point between the Housing Law and the Law on Real Estate Business. The committee also recommends clarifying the relationship between publishing standard contracts and the standard contract registration procedure under consumer protection law.
5. Project transfers: authority moves to the provincial People's Committee
For projects whose investment policy was approved by the Prime Minister, the draft assigns the
provincial People's Committee

to decide whether to permit the transfer of all or part of a project. The developer remains responsible for its commitments after approval. The examination committee recommends further study of cases where the developer cannot continue and a capable party takes over and inherits the financial obligations. In that case, the rights of customers who have already purchased need to be clearly protected.
6. Transaction process and electronic identification codes
The draft adds a framework for the transaction process and
electronic identification codes

for organizations, individuals and each property. The examination committee recommends that expanding the types of contracts that can be transferred be included in the law only once the practical basis and risk controls are clarified.
Current law vs. the draft
Scale
— Law on Real Estate Business 29/2023/QH15 (in force): 83 articles; Draft Law on Real Estate Business (amended), submitted to the National Assembly on 22 October 2026: 10 chapters, 61 articles
Deposit for off-plan homes

— Law on Real Estate Business 29/2023/QH15 (in force): At most 5% of the sale price, only once business conditions are met (Clause 5, Article 23); Draft Law on Real Estate Business (amended), submitted to the National Assembly on 22 October 2026: Keeps the 5% cap (July 2026 draft); recommended to be separated from capital mobilization
Payments before a certificate is issued

— Law on Real Estate Business 29/2023/QH15 (in force): First payment ≤ 30% (including the deposit); before handover ≤ 70% (≤ 50% if the seller is a foreign-invested enterprise); before the certificate is issued ≤ 95% (Article 25); Draft Law on Real Estate Business (amended), submitted to the National Assembly on 22 October 2026: Adds a security mechanism for the remaining 5% via a blocked account or by agreement
Bank guarantee

— Law on Real Estate Business 29/2023/QH15 (in force): Mandatory before sale (Article 26); Draft Law on Real Estate Business (amended), submitted to the National Assembly on 22 October 2026: Still mandatory (Article 20 of the July 2026 draft)
Notarization

— Law on Real Estate Business 29/2023/QH15 (in force): At request if one party is a real estate business enterprise; mandatory if the parties are individuals (Clauses 4, 5, Article 44); Draft Law on Real Estate Business (amended), submitted to the National Assembly on 22 October 2026: Kept similar; the scope is being recommended for review
Authority to transfer projects approved by the Prime Minister

— Law on Real Estate Business 29/2023/QH15 (in force): Prime Minister (may delegate to the provincial People's Committee for partial transfers) (Article 41); Draft Law on Real Estate Business (amended), submitted to the National Assembly on 22 October 2026: Provincial People's Committee
Effect

— Law on Real Estate Business 29/2023/QH15 (in force): From 1 August 2024; Draft Law on Real Estate Business (amended), submitted to the National Assembly on 22 October 2026: 2027, no specific date stated (Article 60 of the July 2026 draft)
What homebuyers should note
A contract signed today is still governed by
. Under the draft, contracts established before the new law takes effect continue to be performed under the old law.
Only pay a deposit when the project
meets the conditions to be put on sale
, and do not pay more than 5% of the sale price.
Ask for a copy of the
bank guarantee commitment
when signing an off-plan home purchase contract.
Compare the payment schedule against the 30% / 70% / 95% thresholds of current law.
Look up the standard contract and project information the developer has published before signing.
Follow the National Assembly's vote result before believing any "new regulation" cited by the seller.
Reference documents
Law on Real Estate Business No. 29/2023/QH15
, National Assembly, dated 28 November 2023 (effective from 1 August 2024 under Law No. 43/2024/QH15). Look up at: https://vanban.chinhphu.vn/?pageid=27160&docid=209624
Draft dossier of the Law on Real Estate Business (amended)
, Ministry of Construction, posted for comment in July 2026: https://moc.gov.vn/vn/pages/chitietduthao.aspx?iDuThao=1004
Resolution No. 278/NQ-CP dated 18 September 2026
of the Government: https://xaydungchinhsach.chinhphu.vn/chinh-phu-yeu-cau-khan-truong-hoan-thien-cac-du-an-luat-dat-dai-nha-o-kinh-doanh-bat-dong-san-sua-doi-119260920101326422.htm
Preliminary examination

, Committee on Economic and Financial Affairs, 29 September 2026 (People's Representative Newspaper): https://daibieunhandan.vn/tham-tra-so-bo-du-an-luat-dat-dai-sua-doi-va-du-an-luat-kinh-doanh-bat-dong-san-sua-doi-10432172.html
Submission and examination report presented to the National Assembly on 22 October 2026

(Government Electronic Portal): https://xaydungchinhsach.chinhphu.vn/du-an-luat-kinh-doanh-bat-dong-san-sua-doi-de-nghi-mo-rong-cac-loai-hop-dong-duoc-chuyen-nhuong-119261022093700874.htm and https://baochinhphu.vn/quoc-hoi-nghe-bao-cao-ve-2-du-an-luat-nha-o-sua-doi-va-luat-kinh-doanh-bat-dong-san-sua-doi-102261022090050259.htm
Press Release No. 06, 2nd Session, 16th National Assembly
(People's Representative Newspaper), 22 October 2026: https://daibieunhandan.vn/thong-cao-bao-chi-so-06-ky-hop-thu-2-quoc-hoi-khoa-xvi-10439539.html

This article is general information compiled from legal documents and publicly available drafts and does not replace legal advice. The content of the draft may change when the National Assembly adopts it. Updated on 23 October 2026.

Luật Quy hoạch đô thị và nông thôn: cách.title: Law on Urban and Rural Planning: How to Check the Planning Before You Commit Money
Luật Quy hoạch đô thị và nông thôn: cách.excerpt: How many planning levels there are, what the public may view, and where to look it up in Hanoi. A guide to checking the planning under the new law before buying a home.
content: Before putting down a deposit on an apartment or a plot of land, the first question to ask is: what is this place designated for under the planning? Since 1 July 2025, the preparation and management of urban planning has been governed by the
Law on Urban and Rural Planning No. 47/2024/QH15
. This law was amended by
dated 11 December 2025 and is guided by
Decree No. 178/2025/NĐ-CP
This article briefly explains what the law provides, what buyers are entitled to see, and the steps for checking the planning in Hanoi.
Three documents to know

was adopted by the National Assembly on 26 November 2024 and took effect on 1 July 2025. It replaces the old terms "construction planning" and "urban planning" with a single system called urban and rural planning.

dated 11 December 2025 amends and supplements a number of articles of Law No. 47, effective from 1 January 2026. Earlier, Law No. 47 had also been partly amended by the Law on Digital Technology Industry, No. 71/2025/QH15.
Decree No. 178/2025/NĐ-CP
dated 1 July 2025 provides detailed regulations for the law. This decree was amended by
Decree No. 34/2026/NĐ-CP
dated 22 January 2026.
What does Law No. 144/2025/QH15 change?
According to the consolidated text by the Office of the National Assembly, the notable amendments include:
Amending the types of planning and adding planning for
special zones
, in line with the two-level local government model.
Repealing some articles and clauses of the original law, including Article 24 and Article 28.
Drawing scales
of master plans, zoning plans and detailed plans are no longer fixed in the law but are assigned to the
Minister of Construction
to regulate.
The planning specialist agencies under the
commune People's Committee
are also responsible for providing planning information, together with provincial agencies and functional zone management units.

Adding a temporary mechanism (Article 2 of Law No. 144, applicable from 1 January 2026 to the end of 28 February 2027): zoning plans for urban areas formed after the administrative unit reorganization are prepared in parallel and may be approved before the provincial plan or master plan.
How many planning levels are there?
The law divides urban and rural planning into
three levels
: master planning, zoning planning and detailed planning (Clause 3, Article 3). The further down the levels, the closer the information is to individual land lots.
Master plan

Prepared for cities, urban areas, communes, economic zones, national tourist areas and special zones. This is the strategic picture: which direction the urban area develops in and what the main infrastructure framework looks like. A master plan cannot answer the question "what can be built on this lot".
Zoning plan
Prepared for each area within the master plan. Under Article 25, a zoning plan sets population, land use and technical infrastructure indicators
for each city block
, and arranges schools, parks and social housing (if any). This is the layer to look at to know what will be around the project.
Detailed plan
Under Article 26, a detailed plan specifies the
function and land use indicators for each land lot

, the spatial organization, infrastructure and urban design. The market still commonly calls it "1/500 planning" after the drawing scale commonly used before. Under current law, the drawing scale is set by the Minister of Construction.
One more case to know: under Article 10 of Decree 178 (as amended), some small projects do not have to prepare a full detailed plan but prepare a
"site master plan"

. For example, an apartment building project under 2 ha, located in an area with an approved zoning plan, carried out by a single developer. The site master plan must be approved in writing by a competent authority. When asking for documents, buyers should know which case the project falls under.
What can the public view?
The law is fairly clear:
Mandatory announcement (Article 50):

within 15 days at the latest after approval, the plan must be publicly announced. The announcement dossier includes the approval decision, drawings, explanatory report and planning management regulations. Announcements are made at agency offices, on web portals and on the national planning information system.
Right of access (Clause 1, Article 55):

every organization and individual may access approved and announced plans, planning management regulations, implementation plans for master plans, administrative procedures and legal documents on planning.
Provision on request (Clauses 2 and 3, Article 55):
provincial and commune-level specialist agencies must provide approved planning information on request and
are responsible for the accuracy
of the documents they provide. Information may be provided by direct explanation or in writing.
Boundary markers (Article 52):
red lines, construction-prohibited zone boundaries and so on are marked out on the ground.
Note: Law No. 47/2024 does not provide for a procedure called a "planning certificate" as it was commonly known before. Currently, people ask the competent authority to
provide planning information
. Before submitting, it is advisable to ask the receiving agency directly about the required documents and the response time.
Summary table
Master plan
— Question it answers: Which direction the urban area develops in; What buyers should look at: Regional orientation, major transport axes
Zoning plan
— Question it answers: What each city block is used for, density, population; What buyers should look at: Schools, green space, planned roads around the project
Detailed plan / site master plan
— Question it answers: What can be built on each lot and how high; What buyers should look at: The approval decision or approval document, the function of the lot of the home you are buying
Steps to check planning in Hanoi
Look on the website of the Hanoi Department of Planning and Architecture
(https://qhkt.hanoi.gov.vn), in the "Công bố quy hoạch" (Planning Announcements) section. This is where the Department posts approved plans.
Request official information in writing

when you need it for a transaction. Send your request to the Department of Planning and Architecture (31B Tràng Thi) or the ward or commune People's Committee where the lot is located. Under the law, the providing agency is responsible for the accuracy of the information.
Distinguish it from land use planning.

The city has a lookup page for land use planning and plans (https://qhkhsdd.hanoi.gov.vn). This is information in the land sector, different from urban planning. Online lookup results are for reference only; when you need them for a transaction, request a written information document from the competent authority.
Do not pay for unofficial lookup services.

In July 2026, the Department of Planning and Architecture advised residents not to use or pay fees to unofficial planning lookup sites and groups. According to the Department, the planning database is expected to be largely completed by the end of 2026 and then made public on an official platform.
Ask the developer to present
the decision approving the project's detailed plan (or the document approving the site master plan). Compare the function of the lot with the type of product being offered for sale.
What homebuyers should do
Identify which zoning plan the lot falls under, and whether a detailed plan or site master plan has been approved.
Ask for a copy of the approval decision with the drawings, not just the advertising renderings.
Check that the function of the lot is indeed residential land or housing, as the product being sold.
Ask about planned roads and red lines adjoining the project boundary.
When you need certainty, send a written request for planning information to the state agency.
Keep the number and date of every document to cross-check when signing the contract.
The projects Tami distributes in the Ciputra urban area, Phú Thượng Ward, such as Maison Privée, Astor 1 and The Windsor Collection, can all be cross-checked following the steps above. You can
contact Tami to review the legal file of each project
Reference documents
Law on Urban and Rural Planning No. 47/2024/QH15

dated 26 November 2024, National Assembly, effective 1 July 2025. Consolidated text by the Office of the National Assembly (including amendments in Law No. 71/2025/QH15 and Law No. 144/2025/QH15), published on the Government Electronic Portal: https://datafiles.chinhphu.vn/cpp/files/vbpq/2026/3/33-vbhn-vpqh.pdf

dated 11 December 2025, National Assembly, amending and supplementing a number of articles of the Law on Urban and Rural Planning, effective 1 January 2026 (content looked up via the consolidated text above).
Law on Digital Technology Industry, No. 71/2025/QH15
dated 14 June 2025, National Assembly (partly amending Law No. 47/2024/QH15).
Decree No. 178/2025/NĐ-CP
dated 1 July 2025, Government, detailing a number of articles of the Law on Urban and Rural Planning; amended by
Decree No. 34/2026/NĐ-CP
dated 22 January 2026. Consolidated document No. 18/VBHN-BXD dated 24 March 2026 of the Ministry of Construction: https://moc.gov.vn/Images/FileVanBan/BXD_18-VBHN-BXD_24032026.pdf
Website of the Hanoi Department of Planning and Architecture: https://qhkt.hanoi.gov.vn
This article is general information compiled from legal documents and does not replace legal advice. Updated on 23 October 2026.

Mua căn hộ hình thành trong tương lai: 5.title: Buying an Off-Plan Apartment: 5 Things to Check Under the 2023 Law on Real Estate Business
Mua căn hộ hình thành trong tương lai: 5.excerpt: Buying an apartment that is not finished yet? 5 points to review under the 2023 Law on Real Estate Business: sales eligibility document, guarantee, deposit, payments, mortgage.
content: Buying an apartment while the project is still under construction (which the law calls
housing formed in the future
) gives buyers better prices and a more comfortable payment schedule. In return, the buyer pays for an asset that does not yet exist, so the risk is higher than buying a ready-made home.
Law on Real Estate Business No. 29/2023/QH15
(in force from 1 August 2024 under Law No. 43/2024/QH15) and
Decree No. 96/2024/NĐ-CP
set out many safeguards to protect buyers. Below are 5 points to check yourself before committing money.
Quick summary
Document confirming the housing is eligible for sale
— Legal milestone: The provincial agency responds within 15 days; Basis: Article 24 of the 2023 Law on Real Estate Business; Article 8 of Decree 96/2024
Bank guarantee
— Legal milestone: Receive the guarantee letter before making any payment; Basis: Article 26 of the 2023 Law on Real Estate Business
Deposit
— Legal milestone: At most 5% of the sale price, only once business conditions are met; Basis: Clause 5, Article 23 of the 2023 Law on Real Estate Business
Payment schedule

— Legal milestone: First payment ≤ 30%; before handover ≤ 70% (≤ 50% if the seller has foreign investment capital); before the certificate is issued ≤ 95%; Basis: Article 25 of the 2023 Law on Real Estate Business
Contract and mortgage

— Legal milestone: Contract in the Government's standard form; a mortgaged project or apartment must be released from the mortgage before signing; Basis: Article 44 of the 2023 Law on Real Estate Business; Clause 2, Article 183 of the 2023 Housing Law
1. Document confirming the housing is eligible for sale
Under Article 24 of the 2023 Law on Real Estate Business, off-plan housing may be put on sale only when it meets this group of conditions:
Construction has started.
It has one of the documents on land use rights (a decision on land allocation, land lease, or permission to change the land use purpose, or a Certificate).

It has a construction permit (if one is required) and a technical infrastructure acceptance record according to the schedule. For apartment buildings or mixed-use buildings with housing, it must have a record of
foundation completion acceptance
It belongs to a project approved for construction for sale or lease-purchase.
Most important is
Clause 4, Article 24
: before selling, the developer must send a written notice to the provincial state management agency for real estate business (in Hanoi, the Department of Construction). That agency has
15 days
to check and reply in writing on whether the housing is eligible or not. Detailed dossiers and procedures are in Article 8 of Decree No. 96/2024/NĐ-CP.
How to check:
ask the developer or distributor to show you the Department of Construction's reply, and match the project name, building and number of units for sale exactly.
2. Bank guarantee

Article 26 of the 2023 Law on Real Estate Business requires the developer to obtain a guarantee commitment from a domestic commercial bank or a foreign bank branch before selling. If the developer fails to hand over the home as committed, the bank performs the financial obligation instead, including the money the buyer has paid in advance and other amounts under the contract.
Three points buyers need to remember:
When signing the contract, the developer must hand over a
copy of the bank's guarantee commitment document
(Clause 2).
The buyer
may choose
whether or not to receive the guarantee; if not, this must be clearly stated in the contract (Clause 3).
The developer must hand over the guarantee letter within 10 working days of signing (or another period agreed by the parties) and
may only collect money after the buyer has received the guarantee letter
(Clause 6).
The guarantee rule does not apply to social housing (Clause 8).
3. Deposit: at most 5% and at the right time
Clause 5, Article 23 of the 2023 Law on Real Estate Business provides that the developer may collect a deposit of
no more than 5% of the sale or lease-purchase price
, and only when the housing
meets the conditions to be put on sale
. The deposit agreement must clearly state the sale or lease-purchase price.

In other words, if the project does not yet have the eligibility document from item 1, "reservations" or "deposits" that take money from buyers are a warning sign. Clause 4, Article 23 also prohibits the developer from authorizing another party to sign a deposit agreement or a sale contract.
4. Limits on each payment installment
Article 25 of the 2023 Law on Real Estate Business sets a ceiling on collecting money:
First payment
(including the deposit): no more than
of the contract value.
Later payments
according to the construction schedule, totaling no more than
before handover. If the seller is an economic organization with foreign investment capital, this level is
When the buyer has not yet been issued a Certificate
: the seller collects no more than
. The remainder is paid once the state agency has issued the Certificate.
For lease-purchase, the first payment is also no more than 30%, and total advance payments until handover are no more than 50%.
How to check:
add up the payment schedule in the contract, see whether any installment exceeds the ceiling, and whether it is tied to actual construction progress.
5. Standard contract, notarization and mortgage
Contract:

Clause 7, Article 44 of the 2023 Law on Real Estate Business assigns the Government to issue standard contracts. The current templates are in the appendices to Decree No. 96/2024/NĐ-CP. When one party is a real estate business enterprise (usually the developer), notarization or certification of the contract is
as agreed by the parties
, not mandatory (Clause 4). A sale contract between two individuals must be notarized or certified (Clause 5).
Mortgage:

Clause 1, Article 183 of the 2023 Housing Law allows the developer to mortgage part or all of the project, or housing within the project, at a credit institution to borrow capital for that same project. However, under Clause 2, Article 183, if it wants to sell or lease-purchase mortgaged housing, the developer must
release
that part of the project or that housing together with the land use rights from the mortgage
before signing the contract

with the customer (the law has separate exceptions for certain social housing cases in Article 88). That the housing has been released from the mortgage is clearly stated in the notice of housing eligible for sale issued by the provincial housing management agency, and the developer must hand this document to the customer when signing the contract. Buyers should read that document carefully to know whether the apartment they choose has been released from the mortgage.
What homebuyers should do
View the Department of Construction's document confirming the housing is eligible for sale, matching the project name and building.
Receive a copy of the guarantee commitment when signing the contract; with no guarantee letter yet, make no payment (unless you chose to forgo the guarantee and this is stated in the contract).
Do not pay a deposit above 5%, and do not pay a deposit when the project does not yet meet business conditions.
Review the payment schedule: first payment ≤ 30%, before handover ≤ 70%, with at least 5% held back until you receive the certificate.
Compare the contract with the template in Decree No. 96/2024/NĐ-CP; terms that differ from the template should be clearly explained.
Check in the eligibility-for-sale notice whether the apartment has been released from the mortgage.
Make sure the deposit agreement and sale contract are signed by the developer itself, not by a party "authorized to sign".

If you are interested in the projects Tami Homes distributes in the Ciputra – Phú Thượng area, you can ask Tami to provide each project's legal file so you can cross-check against the checklist above.
Note:

On 22 October 2026, the Government submitted the draft amended Law on Real Estate Business and the draft amended Housing Law to the National Assembly (2nd Session, 16th term). As of 23 October 2026, these two drafts had
not yet been voted on and adopted
, so the regulations above still apply. Some regulations may change once the new laws are adopted and take effect.
Reference documents
Law on Real Estate Business No. 29/2023/QH15
dated 28 November 2023, National Assembly: https://vanban.chinhphu.vn/?pageid=27160&docid=209624

dated 29 June 2024, National Assembly, amending the Land Law, Housing Law, Law on Real Estate Business and Law on Credit Institutions (bringing the 2023 Law on Real Estate Business into force from 1 August 2024): https://vanban.chinhphu.vn/?pageid=27160&docid=211201
Housing Law No. 27/2023/QH15
dated 27 November 2023, National Assembly (Article 183 on mortgage): https://vanban.chinhphu.vn/?pageid=27160&docid=209627
Decree No. 96/2024/NĐ-CP
dated 24 July 2024, Government, detailing a number of articles of the Law on Real Estate Business (as amended by Decree No. 54/2026/NĐ-CP): https://vanban.chinhphu.vn/?pageid=27160&docid=210798
Press Release No. 06, 2nd Session, 16th National Assembly
(People's Representative Newspaper), 22 October 2026: https://daibieunhandan.vn/thong-cao-bao-chi-so-06-ky-hop-thu-2-quoc-hoi-khoa-xvi-10439539.html
This article is general information compiled from legal documents and does not replace legal advice. Updated on 23 October 2026.

Nghị định 54/2026/NĐ-CP: điểm mới về nhà.title: Decree No. 54/2026/NĐ-CP: What's New on Social Housing and Real Estate Trading Floors
Nghị định 54/2026/NĐ-CP: điểm mới về nhà.excerpt: Decree No. 54/2026/NĐ-CP amends 6 decrees on housing and real estate business: simpler social housing procedures, and trading floors that cease operating must notify the Department of Construction.
content: On 9 February 2026, the Government issued
Decree No. 54/2026/NĐ-CP

amending and supplementing a number of articles of decrees in the fields of housing and real estate business. The document took effect immediately on the date of signing (Clause 1, Article 41), has no retroactive effect and does not replace any document.
This is a technical revision: less paperwork, clearer processing deadlines, and more authority delegated to localities.
Which documents does Decree 54/2026 amend?
According to information provided by the Ministry of Construction in Official Dispatch 3511/BXD-QLN dated 5 March 2026, the Decree has 43 articles in 6 chapters and amends six decrees:

— Main content: Guidance on the Law on Real Estate Business; Notable change: Electronic dossiers; trading floors and brokerage enterprises that terminate or suspend operations do so under enterprise law and must notify the Department of Construction
— Main content: Guidance on the Housing Law; Notable change: Adds Article 37a on the sale, lease and lease-purchase prices of State-invested resettlement housing

— Main content: Renovation and reconstruction of apartment buildings; Notable change: Shorter procedures; allows a bidding process to select the developer when agreement on receiving the transfer of land use rights cannot be reached

— Main content: Development and management of social housing; Notable change: Changes the agency that confirms housing and income conditions; clarifies the purchase registration sequence; gives priority in sales to current tenants

— Main content: Delineation of authority under the two-level local government; Notable change: Commune People's Committees are decentralized or authorized to act as owner representative of public-asset housing
— Main content: Decentralization and delegation by the Ministry of Construction; Notable change: Adds authority over public-service housing projects
Social housing: changes applicants need to know
Social housing is the part revised the most (Chapter IV, amending Decree No. 100/2024/NĐ-CP).
Confirmation of "not owning a home" is done by the certificate-issuing agency

Article 32 of Decree 54/2026 amends Clause 1, Article 29 of Decree 100/2024. An applicant is considered not to own housing when neither they nor their spouse (if any) are named in, or have housing information in, a Certificate in the province or city where the project is located. The confirmation is done by the
competent authority that issues Certificates
in that locality, within
7 days
of receiving the request form.
Workers without a labor contract: commune Police confirm income
Article 33 amends Clause 2, Article 30 of Decree 100/2024 for low-income urban residents (Clause 5, Article 76 of the Housing Law)
without a labor contract
, such as freelancers. What is new:
The confirming agency is the
commune Police
where the person has permanent residence, temporary residence or current residence, within
7 days
The applicant declares and commits to their average monthly income; the commune Police may coordinate verification and post-checks when needed.
The income confirmation application
also serves as the document proving eligibility
, so freelancers do not need to request a separate eligibility confirmation.
Note: the income ceiling in Clause 1, Article 30 was later further amended by
Decree No. 136/2026/NĐ-CP
(effective 7 April 2026), which is not part of Decree 54. Applicants should consult the latest consolidated text (Consolidated Document 24/VBHN-BXD dated 18 May 2026) before submitting a dossier.
A clearer purchase registration sequence
Article 34 rewrites Article 38 of Decree 100/2024. Some points buyers need to know:
The developer must publish information at least
30 days
before accepting dossiers; the dossier acceptance period is at least
30 days
Each household or individual
may not register for multiple projects
at the same time.
Documents proving eligibility and conditions are valid for
12 months
from the date of confirmation. Applicants must commit that they have not yet benefited from a housing support policy.
The developer publishes the list of eligible dossiers within
30 days
of the submission deadline.
Priority for women applies only when the applicant is a single woman or the household head according to residence data.
Current tenants get priority to buy before the 10-year term
Article 38 amends Clause 12, Article 78 of Decree 100/2024. For social housing
leased under Clause 2, Article 26 of Decree No. 100/2015/NĐ-CP
, the developer may give priority in sales to the
current tenant

if they wish to buy before the 10-year term and meet the eligibility and conditions. The developer may also sell back to the National Housing Fund. The sale price is calculated from the appraised price, plus average loan interest over the lease period, less depreciation.
This is a transitional provision for a specific group of projects and does not apply generally to every social housing unit currently being leased.
Trading floors and brokerage enterprises
For Decree No. 96/2024/NĐ-CP, the direction of the amendment is
cutting conditions and increasing transparency
Article 6
amends Point b, Clause 4, Article 17: when a trading floor terminates or suspends operations, it does so under enterprise law. The notice must
also be sent to the Department of Construction
for public posting.
Article 7
amends Article 18: a brokerage enterprise only needs to meet the conditions on head office and business location under enterprise law.
Article 8
adds
Article 18a
on termination and suspension of operations of brokerage enterprises, who must likewise notify the Department of Construction.
Repeals Clause 2, Article 15, Clause 6, Article 26 (dossiers for the brokerage practice certificate exam) and Point c, Clause 9, Article 31.
As a result, buyers can check the Department of Construction's information page to see whether a trading floor is still operating before transacting.
Resettlement housing prices and apartment renovation
Article 37a
(added to Decree 95/2024 by Article 19 of Decree 54): the sale price of State-invested resettlement housing is decided by the
provincial People's Committee
(or the commune level if decentralized), on the principle of calculating costs correctly and fully. Lease and lease-purchase prices are calculated by the formula in this article.
Apartment renovation

(Chapter III): the provincial People's Committee decides the maximum time for agreeing on the transfer of land use rights; if no agreement is reached, a bidding process is held to select the developer.
Transition: what about dossiers already submitted?
Dossiers submitted before 9 February 2026: the receiving agency may not require additional documents that the new Decree has dropped, unless the relevant database is not yet operational.
Social housing projects that
have already received dossiers
under Decree 100/2024 continue under the old sequence; projects that
have not yet received dossiers
apply the new regulations.
Eligibility confirmations issued before 9 February 2026 remain usable for
12 months
from the date of confirmation.
What homebuyers should do
Check whether the social housing project began accepting dossiers before or after 9 February 2026 to know which sequence applies.
If you are a freelancer, contact the commune Police where you reside to confirm your income; keep your declaration truthful because it may be post-checked.
Track the issue date of your confirmation, because it is valid for only 12 months.
Register for only
one
social housing project at a time.
Before transacting through a trading floor, check the Department of Construction's information page to see whether the floor is still operating or has terminated or suspended operations.

If you are looking into commercial housing in the Ciputra – Phú Thượng area, you can also see information on the projects Tami Homes distributes, such as Maison Privée, Astor 1 and The Windsor Collection, on the website.
Reference documents
Decree No. 54/2026/NĐ-CP
dated 9 February 2026, Government, amending and supplementing a number of articles of Decrees in the fields of housing and real estate business. Look up at:
Government Gazette
or
Government Electronic Portal
Official Dispatch No. 3511/BXD-QLN
dated 5 March 2026, Ministry of Construction, providing information on legal documents issued in February 2026:
moc.gov.vn
Consolidated Document No. 24/VBHN-BXD
dated 18 May 2026, Ministry of Construction, consolidating Decree 100/2024/NĐ-CP on social housing:
moc.gov.vn
Consolidated Document No. 20/VBHN-BXD

dated 26 March 2026, Ministry of Construction, consolidating Decree 98/2024/NĐ-CP on renovation and reconstruction of apartment buildings: [moc.gov.vn](https://moc.gov.vn/Images/FileVanBan/BXD_20-VBHN-BXD_26032026(1).pdf)
Decree No. 136/2026/NĐ-CP
dated 7 April 2026, Government, amending Decree 100/2024/NĐ-CP (income conditions):
Government Gazette
or
Government Electronic Portal
This article is general information compiled from legal documents and does not replace legal advice. Updated on 23 October 2026.

Nghị quyết 254/2025/QH15: những thay đổi.title: Resolution No. 254/2025/QH15: Land Changes Applying from 1 January 2026
Nghị quyết 254/2025/QH15: những thay đổi.excerpt: From 1 January 2026, land prices are calculated using the land price list and adjustment coefficient, and there are new cases of land recovery. A summary of what homebuyers need to know.
content: The 2024 Land Law had been running for more than a year when the National Assembly issued a further resolution to clear obstacles in its application. That is
Resolution No. 254/2025/QH15
, adopted on 11 December 2025 at the 10th session, in force from
1 January 2026

. It is a short document of only 13 articles, but it touches on matters homebuyers often face: how land prices are calculated, when the State recovers land, how much it costs to convert garden land to residential land, and certificate issuance for buyers.
This article summarizes the main points according to the original text, together with the Government's guidance in
Decree No. 49/2026/NĐ-CP
How does Resolution 254 fit with the Land Law?

The Resolution does not replace the Land Law. It adds certain separate mechanisms for the places that are hard to implement. There is an important principle in Clause 3, Article 13: while the resolution is in force, if the resolution and a law provide differently on the same matter,
the resolution applies
So when reading a land regulation in 2026, buyers need to look at both the Land Law and Resolution 254, not just one document.
1. Land prices: the land price list and adjustment coefficient take center stage
This is the change with the widest impact.
The provincial People's Council decides the land price list
Under Clause 3, Article 7, the
provincial People's Council

decides the land price list, announced and applied from 1 January 2026, and amended and supplemented when needed. The list is prepared by land type, area and location. Where a digital cadastral map and a land price database exist, it can be prepared down to individual parcels (Clause 2, Article 7).

The land price list is the basis for many things (Clause 1, Article 7): calculating land use fees and land rent upon land allocation, land lease, change of purpose and recognition of land use rights; auction starting prices; calculating taxes, fees and charges related to land use; administrative fines; and compensation when the State recovers land.
The provincial People's Committee issues the land price adjustment coefficient
Article 8 defines the land price adjustment coefficient as the
rate of increase or decrease in land price
relative to the price in the land price list, by land type, area and location. The
provincial People's Committee
issues this coefficient, applicable from 1 January each year, and may amend it during the year or for specific areas and locations when needed.
Under Article 5, the price used to calculate land use fees and compensation are both based on the
land price list and adjustment coefficient
. If land is auctioned, the winning auction price is used. A small but practical point: decisions on land allocation, land lease and change of purpose
do not have to state the land price
(Clause 4, Article 5).
The 1 July 2026 deadline
Clause 5, Article 7 requires competent authorities to issue all the bases for calculating land use fees, land rent and compensation
no later than 1 July 2026

. Until the bases are complete, calculations still follow the Land Law. That deadline has now passed. If you have a dossier that gave rise to a financial obligation in the first half of 2026, you should ask the tax authority how your dossier is being calculated.

For cases that should have had a specific land price determined but had no price decision by 1 January 2026, the provincial People's Committee may choose to apply the new method or continue with specific valuation (Clause 4, Article 7).
2. Land recovery, compensation, resettlement

Article 3 adds some cases in which the State recovers land, such as projects in free trade zones and international financial centers. Notable for commercial housing projects: if the developer negotiates on its own to receive land use rights, and after the negotiation period has expired has reached
over 75% of the area and over 75% of the land users

, the provincial People's Council may consider recovering the remainder to allocate it to the developer (Point b, Clause 2, Article 3). Those with land in the remaining portion receive extra payment if their compensation is lower than the average of the agreed prices (Clause 7, Article 3).
On procedure, Clause 9, Article 3 provides:
The recovery notice is sent
at least 60 days
in advance for agricultural land and
120 days
for non-agricultural land.
The compensation plan is posted publicly for
10 days
If there are still objections, a dialogue is held within
no more than 30 days
of the date comments were collected.
Housing that must be fully demolished, or partly demolished with the remainder not meeting technical standards, is compensated at the
new construction value
of the whole building at an equivalent standard (Point a, Clause 11, Article 3).
3. Converting garden and pond land to residential land

For garden land, pond land and agricultural land within the same parcel as residential land, Point c, Clause 2, Article 10 sets the land use fee on the difference between the residential land price and the agricultural land price:
of the difference for the area within the residential land allocation limit;
for the area exceeding the limit but not more than 1 times the limit;
for the area exceeding 1 times the limit.
This rate applies only
once per household or individual

(calculated on 1 parcel). Those who were permitted to change purpose between 1 August 2024 and before 1 January 2026 are recalculated at the new rate. If the recalculated amount is lower than what was paid, the difference is refunded or offset against other obligations (Clause 10, Article 4).
4. Certificates (red book), parcel splitting and merging
Some points in Article 11 relate directly to buyers:
If the Housing Law or the Law on Real Estate Business sets a deadline for filing a Certificate dossier for the buyer that differs from the deadline for registering changes under the Land Law, then
the Housing Law or the Law on Real Estate Business applies
(Point c, Clause 2).

Splitting or merging parcels requires access to a public road or the consent of the adjoining neighbor to pass through. Residential land set aside as an access way does not have to change purpose. Merged parcels do not have to share the same use purpose (Clause 3).
What does Decree No. 49/2026/NĐ-CP guide?
The Government issued Decree No. 49/2026/NĐ-CP on
31 January 2026
, effective the same day. Some main points:
The land price adjustment coefficient has three types
: by market fluctuation, by planning, and by other factors affecting land prices (Clause 1, Article 8).
The market fluctuation coefficient equals the
market land price divided by the price in the land price list
. The market price is taken from at least 3 sample parcels that have been traded, won at auction or had a price approved (Clause 3, Article 8).
The planning coefficient is calculated by land type and the project's
land use coefficient
(Clause 4, Article 8).

Article 5 lists the cases in which the land price list is not used and a specific valuation is made instead, such as sea reclamation projects or mixed-purpose projects decided by the provincial People's Committee.
Detailed provisions on land use fees and land rent are assigned to
a separate decree
(Clause 2, Article 1). That is
Decree No. 50/2026/NĐ-CP
detailing a number of articles of Resolution 254/2025/QH15 on land use fees and land rent (see Reference documents).
Chapter IV on decentralization and delegation is implemented
through 28 February 2027
(Clause 2, Article 16).
Quick summary
Resolution No. 254/2025/QH15
— Effective date: 1 January 2026; Decided by: National Assembly; Applies to: Mechanisms to clear obstacles in implementing the Land Law
Land price list

— Effective date: Applied from 1 January 2026, amended when needed; Decided by: Provincial People's Council; Applies to: Land use fees, land rent, taxes and fees, compensation, auction starting prices
Land price adjustment coefficient

— Effective date: From 1 January each year, amended during the year when needed; Decided by: Provincial People's Committee; Applies to: Multiplied by the price in the land price list to give the price used for calculation
Issuing all bases for calculation
— Effective date: No later than 1 July 2026; Decided by: Competent local authority; Applies to: Land use fees, land rent, compensation
Decree No. 49/2026/NĐ-CP
— Effective date: 31 January 2026; Decided by: Government; Applies to: Guidance on the price list, coefficients, land recovery, procedures
Chapter IV of Decree 49
— Effective date: Implemented through 28 February 2027; Decided by: Government; Applies to: Decentralization and delegation in land matters
What homebuyers should do
Look up the current
land price list
and
adjustment coefficient
in the province or city where the property is located before working out transaction costs.
For residential land with garden or pond areas: ask clearly about the area within the allocation limit and the 30/50/100% rates before changing the purpose.
For apartments and homes in a project: ask the developer about the status of land allocation, the project's land-related financial obligations and the progress of certificate processing.
If the land lies in an area that may be recovered: follow the recovery notice and the posting period for the compensation plan so you can submit comments in time.
Dossiers that gave rise to obligations in 2026: ask the tax authority what basis it is calculating on.

Quy hoạch tổng thể Thủ đô Hà Nội tầm nhì.title: Hanoi Capital Master Plan with a 100-Year Vision: The Key Points
Quy hoạch tổng thể Thủ đô Hà Nội tầm nhì.excerpt: Decision No. 2512/QĐ-UBND sets a multi-polar, multi-center structure with the Red River as the main axis. A summary of the points homebuyers should know.
content: On 13 May 2026, the Chairman of the Hanoi City People's Committee signed
Decision No. 2512/QĐ-UBND
approving the Hanoi Capital Master Plan with a 100-year vision. Earlier, the City People's Council had adopted this plan in
Resolution No. 03/NQ-HĐND dated 28 March 2026
. The decision took effect immediately on the date of signing.

The document is long, with many economic and social figures. This article selects only the parts directly related to living space: which direction the city will develop in, what the transport infrastructure looks like, and how the West Lake (Hồ Tây) and Red River riverside areas are mentioned.
Scope and timeline
The plan covers the whole of Hanoi's administrative area, comprising
126 commune-level administrative units (51 wards, 75 communes)
, with an area of about
. The planning period is divided into:
Short term:
Medium term:
Long term:
Strategic vision:
100 years.
On population, the decision forecasts about 14–15 million people by 2035, 15–16 million by 2045 and 17–19 million by 2065. After 2085, the population is capped at no more than 20 million.
A "multi-layered, multi-polar, multi-center" structure
The decision clearly states the principle: an urban structure that is "multi-layered, multi-tiered, multi-polar and multi-center", with the
Red River as the principal ecological and cultural landscape axis
. Put simply, Hanoi will no longer pile every function into the central core but will divide them among several poles, each with its own role.
The spatial framework has three groups, each with 9 components:
9 growth poles

The Central pole (the historic inner city and its extension, the right bank of the Red River), the Northern pole tied to Nội Bài airport, the Eastern pole tied to National Highway 5 and logistics, the Southern pole tied to the second airport, the Vân Đình – Đại Nghĩa pole, the Xuân Mai pole, the Hòa Lạc pole, the Sơn Tây – Ba Vì pole, and the
Red River pole
. The Red River pole is defined as a center of culture, finance, commerce and services, and tourism, and as a new driving force of the Capital.
9 major centers
The South Red River, North Red River, Eastern, Sports urban centers, and Phú Xuyên, Vân Đình – Đại Nghĩa, Xuân Mai, Hòa Lạc and Sơn Tây.
9 driving axes
Comprising the major transport axes linking the center with the poles. Two axes carry the name West Lake:
The West Lake – Cổ Loa – Gia Bình airport axis
: connects the center to the Northeast region and Gia Bình airport (Bắc Ninh).
The Thăng Long Boulevard / West Lake – Ba Vì axis
: connects the center to Hòa Lạc and Ba Vì National Park.
The other axes include Nhật Tân – Nội Bài / North Thăng Long – Nội Bài, National Highway 5, National Highway 1A, National Highway 21B/21C, National Highway 6, National Highway 32, and the
Red River Landscape Boulevard
. For the Red River axis, phase 1 focuses on the section from Hồng Hà Bridge to Mễ Sở Bridge.
Ring roads, railways and new bridges
The decision gives each ring road a different role:
Ring Roads 1, 2, 2.5:
the historic inner city area, prioritizing heritage conservation such as the Old Quarter, Hoàn Kiếm Lake and
West Lake
; renovation of old apartment buildings.
Ring Road 3:
restructured on a compact city model, with transit-oriented development (TOD) at major interchanges and limits on private vehicles entering the center.
Ring Road 3.5:
a chain of new urban areas, receiving the population spreading out from inside Ring Road 3.
Ring Road 4:
the economic and urban belt, the "backbone" of the new development phase.
Ring Roads 4.5 and 5:
connect Hanoi with the 5 surrounding provinces.
On railways, the total network length (including urban railways and regional/inter-regional railways) is about
, of which urban railways are about
979 km

. The network is organized in a "ring and radial" pattern, with 2 ring lines. Alongside it is a three-tier system of TOD points: national/regional level (about 5–10 points), city level (about 20–30 points) and area level (about 120–150 points).
The decision also lists the new Red River bridges to be prioritized for investment, including the
Tứ Liên, Trần Hưng Đạo, Ngọc Hồi, Mễ Sở and Hồng Hà bridges
, along with the renovation and widening of Chương Dương Bridge.

One important note: the decision itself states that specific locations, alignments and cross-section sizes will still be studied in later steps (sectoral planning, urban planning, investment projects). So the master plan shows the
direction
, not yet the detailed drawing for each road or each land parcel.
What does the decision say about West Lake, Tây Hồ Tây and the Red River?
The document does not mention Phú Thượng Ward or any specific urban area in this region by name. The directly relevant provisions are:
West Lake and its surroundings

are grouped with the Thăng Long Imperial Citadel, the Old Quarter and the Temple of Literature – Imperial Academy in the heritage and scenic sites group of the historic inner city. New construction here must raise landscape quality and promote heritage value.
Tây Hồ Tây
is one of two sites (along with Mễ Trì) chosen to receive the headquarters of ministries, sectors and central agencies when they relocate out of the historic inner city.
The Hoàn Kiếm Lake – West Lake area
is identified as the Capital's Tourism Center, with emphasis on cultural and heritage tourism and the night-time economy.
The spaces on both sides of the Red River

(between the left and right dikes, within the limits of the central urban area) are oriented to become a backbone axis for landscape and culture, with parks, public spaces and cultural and entertainment facilities. All development on the river floodplain must ensure flood drainage and comply with dike planning.
The Right-Bank Red River urban area
, the region south of the Red River extending west to the Đáy River green belt, is the Capital's political, administrative, cultural and financial headquarters.
Summary table
Signing date, effect
— Under Decision 2512/QĐ-UBND: 13 May 2026, effective from the date of signing
Council basis
— Under Decision 2512/QĐ-UBND: Resolution 03/NQ-HĐND dated 28 March 2026
Scope
— Under Decision 2512/QĐ-UBND: Whole city, about 3,359.84 km², 126 communes/wards (51 wards, 75 communes)
Timeline
— Under Decision 2512/QĐ-UBND: 2035, 2045, 2065, 2085; 100-year vision
Maximum long-term population
— Under Decision 2512/QĐ-UBND: No more than 20 million people (after 2085)
Structure
— Under Decision 2512/QĐ-UBND: Multi-layered, multi-tiered, multi-polar, multi-center; the Red River as the principal axis
Spatial framework
— Under Decision 2512/QĐ-UBND: 9 growth poles, 9 major centers, 9 driving axes
Railways
— Under Decision 2512/QĐ-UBND: About 1,200 km (urban railways about 979 km), "ring and radial" structure
West Lake area
— Under Decision 2512/QĐ-UBND: Inner-city heritage; Tây Hồ Tây receives relocated central agency headquarters
What homebuyers should do
Understand the level correctly: this is a master plan, a general orientation. To know what a specific lot will be used for, you must look at the
zoning plan and detailed plan
of that area.

Follow the next steps: the decision assigns the Department of Planning and Architecture to issue the Planning Management Regulations, advise on the Implementation Plan, and review approved plans and projects to determine which content remains suitable.
Read the original document on the City's official portal, and do not rely on map images circulating online.
For roads, bridges and metro stations near your home: check whether an approved project exists yet, because the master plan has not fixed detailed locations.
Ask the developer for the project's detailed plan approval decision and compare it with the planning information provided by the state agency.
